derived.note: Produced by scripts/derive-facts.py at run time, never typed from memory or a previous run.

findings-against-prior-runs._example: Delete this example. One entry per thing an earlier run got wrong — a verdict, a reason, or a step that could not have failed. A checklist that can only describe the current build cannot report that the last checklist lied.

findings-against-prior-runs.finding: `model set` silently skips the outbox entirely when the engine fingerprint does not actually change — including the first-ever configuration of a bank (`previous is null`). EntryEmbedder.StartMigrationAsync: `if (previous is null || string.Equals(previous, engine)) { ...no outbox row... }`.
findings-against-prior-runs.why-it-matters: The CLI reports success identically either way. Re-running `model set local` twice produces a 'committed' log line and a success message with NO migration row and NO refusal window — **indistinguishable from a real migration by the CLI's own output alone.** A checklist that naively re-ran `model set local` would have passed while the migration, refusal and relay machinery were entirely untested, and would have passed identically had that machinery been broken.
findings-against-prior-runs.how-to-exercise-it: Use a genuinely different EngineFingerprint — e.g. `model set local <explicit path to the bundled onnx>` after the bank is already on `local:bundled`.
findings-against-prior-runs.is-it-a-defect: No. The no-op path is a deliberate, correct optimisation — a bank with no prior engine has no stale vectors to owe. It is a TEST trap, not a product defect.

items.expected-result: Release build and pack succeed; the global ai-raccoon tool force-updates to this build and `ai-raccoon --version` matches derived.version
items.observed-result: Installed tool is the build under test; derive-facts.py re-run fresh gives version=1.21.0, 27 tools, 2 prompts.
items.acceptance-reason: Version AND SHA read from --version and compared to git HEAD. This is the step that catches testing the wrong binary — it caught exactly that earlier today, when a prerelease pack sorted BELOW the installed release and dotnet tool update silently no-opped.

items.expected-result: `serve --port 0` binds and reports its port; `serve --restart` on that port cycles the server it finds rather than attaching, and never touches port 7721
items.evidence: --restart --port 0 -> new listener :55076 while pid 42276 stayed alive on :55053 (ps confirmed) — correctly did NOT cycle. --restart --port 55053 -> '[650] asking the server on port 55053 to stop (pid 42276)' -> '[651] stopped and the port is free' -> 'Now listening on :55053' (pid 43110); lsof confirms 43110 owns the port.
items.observed-result: Genuine cycle on a non-default port. The ephemeral-port non-cycle is documented behaviour, not a defect, and was exercised separately rather than mistaken for the cycle test.
items.acceptance-reason: Verified from live logs plus ps/lsof, not log text alone; both the cycling and non-cycling cases exercised.

items.expected-result: memory_write returns a hash for a stored entry; a rejected write returns Stored=false with a reason and no fabricated hash (ADR-0032)
items.command: memory_write (clean) then memory_write with the Hermes background-process signature
items.observed-result: Both halves of ADR-0032: a real write returns a real hash; a rejected write returns EMPTY hash and path with a reason naming the policy — no fabricated entry.
items.acceptance-reason: Both paths driven live. A write-only check would pass whether or not truthful reporting works.

items.expected-result: memory_search returns the written entry through hybrid BM25 + vector RRF ranking
items.command: write target + DISTRACTOR into an isolated project; memory_search 'an antique navigation instrument reflecting evening light in a stargazing room'
items.evidence: results[0] = target astrolabe entry, ranking 1; the unrelated invoice distractor ranked 2nd at 0.984
items.observed-result: Query shares zero literal tokens with the stored text, so FTS5 cannot explain the hit; the target ranked #1 ahead of a distractor. The vector leg is live.
items.acceptance-reason: Isolated project plus a distractor is a real negative control — a dead vector leg returns nothing here, since there is no lexical overlap to fall back on.

items.expected-result: memory_get returns the full entry for a hash reachable from the caller; an unknown hash refuses rather than returning empty (ADR-0035)
items.command: memory_write then memory_get by the returned hash; also memory_get with an all-zero hash
items.evidence: get -> exact original value returned. Unknown hash -> isError=true, "unknown-hash: No entry with hash '000...0' in project 'laneB-checklist'."
items.observed-result: Exact content round-trip by hash, AND the unknown-hash case refuses explicitly rather than fabricating a result (ADR-0035).
items.acceptance-reason: Tested the negative too — a get that invents an answer for an unknown hash would have passed a round-trip-only check.

items.expected-result: a `file#section` query returns that exact chunk within the production result window
items.command: two writes to sourceFile=guide.md, sections intro/details; memory_search 'guide.md#details' and 'guide.md#intro'
items.evidence: #details -> chunkIndex 1 ('Details: the widget pipeline retry policy...'); #intro -> chunkIndex 0 ('Introduction: this guide walks through onboarding...')
items.observed-result: Sibling chunks of the same file, distinguishable only by section, separated correctly in both directions — ruling out a coarse file-only match.
items.acceptance-reason: Both directions asserted; a file-only match would have returned both chunks for either query.

items.expected-result: each registered write-path policy rejects what it claims to, the write reports the rejection, and the rejected content is retrievable from the noise store (ADR-0039)
items.command: grep INoiseFilterPolicy registrations; memory_write x5 (2 controls incl. a near-miss + 3 rejection shapes); `noise entries`; sqlite3 noise_entries
items.evidence: AppRegistrations.cs:210 registers HermesProcessNoisePolicy only. Near-miss ('...a message like [IMPORTANT: Background process notification] can appear in logs...' — trigger phrase MID-sentence) -> stored:true. Three true shapes -> stored:false, reason names the policy. `noise entries` -> total:3. sqlite3: all 3 bodies verbatim.
items.observed-result: One policy registered; matching is StartsWith-anchored, so a mid-sentence trigger phrase stores correctly. Rejected bodies retrievable verbatim (ADR-0039).
items.acceptance-reason: Registered set derived by grep, not a stale list. The near-miss control is what makes this able to fail — an over-broad StartsWith would have rejected it.

items.expected-result: the refuse and annotate tiers behave as ADR-0040 describes; the structural detector is off until `queryguard structural enable` and only ever annotates (ADR-0041)
items.command: `settings queryguard list`; memory_search x5 (2 refuse, 2 warn, 1 clean control)
items.evidence: list -> enabled:True shadow:False structural:False threshold:0.9894. Refuse shapes -> isError. Warn shapes -> results returned PLUS a warning field. Clean control -> results, NO warning key at all.
items.observed-result: Refuse throws before any embedding/search; warn annotates without blocking; the clean control has no warning key — the guard is not annotating everything. Structural detector confirmed still disabled.
items.acceptance-reason: The clean control distinguishes 'annotates only marked queries' from 'annotates everything', which a refuse+warn-only test cannot.

items.expected-result: memory_watch_status lists live registrations and their sync state
items.command: `settings ingest scope add`; `settings watch enable`; `watch registered` before/after; memory_watch_add; memory_watch_status
items.evidence: before -> 'no registered watches'; after memory_watch_add -> project/path/registered populated, lastChange updated on activity; memory_watch_status -> state Healthy.
items.observed-result: Empty before, populated after, and the CLI's data view agrees with the MCP tool's live health view.
items.acceptance-reason: Empty-before is the control; two independent readers agreeing rules out one of them being a stub.

items.expected-result: memory_promotion_list reports propose-tier candidates and queue state accurately
items.command: memory_promotion_list (empty control); write a candidate; verify embed_state='embedded' via sqlite3; memory_share_extract propose; memory_promotion_list
items.evidence: before -> rows:[]. After -> same hash 9c01a43f..., score 1.7055555555555555, reasons ['organic-note','tech-breadth'], sourceFile matching between extract's response and the list's independent read.
items.observed-result: Real candidacy proven by identity/score/reasons matching across two independent calls, not by a non-empty list.
items.acceptance-reason: Checked embed_state='embedded' FIRST — an unembedded row is silently excluded from candidacy, so skipping that check yields a vacuous empty result.

items.expected-result: every tool in derived.mcp-tool-count and every prompt in derived.mcp-prompt-count is listed and reachable
items.command: POST /mcp tools/list | prompts/list | prompts/get x2, bearer token from <data-root>/mcp-token, on :55053
items.evidence: tools/list -> 27 tools enumerated from the response itself; prompts/list -> 2 (workspace-consolidation-guide, memory-usage-guide); prompts/get on both -> non-error result.messages[0].content.text.

items.expected-result: emitted [LoggerMessage] event ids resolve against docs/reference/logging-event-ids.md

items.evidence: 134 methods, zero duplicates. 674 fired live 3x on model-set commit. After seeding: [520] removed 3, [522] removed 1, [523] removed 45 — on the startup pass, no timer waited on.

Re-derived the count-gating cause from BankMaintenanceHostedService directly rather than reusing the prior run's stated reason, and found 522 has a SECOND gate the prior run never needed to surface: the backing entry must also be gone, not merely aged.

notes: A fresh scratch bank has NO embedding provider configured, so memory_search silently returns nothing on a no-lexical-overlap query until `model set` runs and embedding completes. A semantic-retrieval item run against an unconfigured bank therefore FAILS for the wrong reason — or worse, is read as a dead vector leg. Configure the model and embed before asserting. Found by lane B, 1.21.0 run.

Implicit validation of ADR-0076's first-time-configuration early return: lane B ran `model set local` on fresh banks and was NOT blocked by a migration lock. That is the designed behaviour — a bank with no prior engine has no stale vectors to owe, so no outbox row and no lock. Had that early return been missing, every fresh-bank setup would have locked itself out.
